## Abstract

source_units.text: 17β-estradiol,the most biologically active estrogen, exerts wide-ranging effects in brain through its action on estrogen receptors (ERs), influencing higher-order cognitive function and neurobiological aging.

## Introduction

Estrogen is a class of steroid hormones that play a key role in the development and regulation of female reproductive system.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Additionally, burgeoning evidence documents that 17β-estradiol (E2), the most biologically active estrogen, exerts wide-ranging effects on neurological and cognitive functions1,2, as well as neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative processes2,3.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: E2 signals through estrogen receptors (ERs) that are ubiquitously distributed in brain1,2 where they coordinate neuroprotective signaling cascades4 and modulate cerebral blood flow, energy metabolism, inflammation, and oxidative processes5,6.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is fundamental for humans, as all women experience a dramatic drop in circulating estradiol as they undergo menopause either through the natural endocrine aging process or through medical intervention7.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Given the extraordinary integrative power of E2 for brain function1,2, it is not surprising that many of the symptoms of menopause are neurological in origin, manifesting as changes in thermoregulation, mood, sleep and cognition3,8.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Hypoestrogenic post-menopausal women are also more vulnerable to brain injury, affective disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's disease (AD)9, which are influenced by ER regulation4.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In translational brain imaging studies, the menopause transition is associated with reduced gray matter volume (GMV) and glucose metabolism10-12, as well as emergence of amyloid-beta (Aβ) plaques, a hallmark of AD, in midlife women11,13.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Post-menopausal GMV and metabolic declines are attenuated by estrogen therapy14,15, suggesting that ER-mediated neurological processes retain dynamic properties well into menopause.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite preclinical evidence of the importance of ERs for neural function and the increasing use of estrogen therapies in clinical practice, our direct knowledge of ER activity in the human brain is very limited.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Positron emission tomography (PET) with selective ER ligands is the only technique currently available that enables in vivo assessment of ER expression.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: 16α-18F-fluoro-17β-estradiol (18F-FES) is the most utilized ER ligand in oncology, exhibiting high binding affinity for ERs, especially ERα16, and excellent signal correlation with ER expression in tumors17,18.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: 18F-FES studies of brain ER expression are instead, scarce.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Animal studies indicate high 18F-FES uptake in brain ER-rich regions, mainly pituitary gland and hypothalamus19-21 and lower yet measurable signal in preoptic area, striatum, amygdala, hippocampus, and cortex22.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This pattern is consistent with the reported distribution of ERs in vitro and ex vivo1,2.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Currently, the only 18F-FES PET study of human brain was conducted in breast cancer patients21.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This study provided important evidence of high tracer uptake in pituitary, with trends toward higher levels in post-menopausal as compared to pre-menopausal patients21.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A few case studies also reported specific 18F-FES signal in pituitary and hypothalamus of breast cancer patients and post-menopausal controls23,24.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

Herein, we took a translational approach to systematically investigate brain ER density and its modulation by neuroendocrine aging using in vivo
18F-FES PET in healthy midlife women.

source_units.text: Additionally, we: (i) conducted multi-modality brain imaging to test for associations of ER density with gray matter volume (GMV), cerebral blood flow (CBF) and mitochondrial adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production in estrogenic regions; and (ii) examined the relationships between ER density and menopausal symptoms of neurological origin.

### ER density by menopause status

## Discussion

This in vivo multi-modality imaging study demonstrates progressively higher brain ER density over the menopause transition, with associated alterations in brain volume, perfusion, and energy metabolism.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Results demonstrate high anatomical overlap with estrogen-regulated brain networks involved in both reproductive function and higher-order cognitive functions, and were independent of chronological age and plasma estradiol (E2) levels.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Elevations in ER density were highly consistent, correctly classifying all post-menopausal women.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, ER density predicted presence of menopause symptoms, chiefly changes in libido, mood, cognition, and vasomotor symptoms.
